text: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial phenomena and the universe at large. One of the foundational concepts in this field is craters, which are large impact features on planets and moons. On the moon, the numerous craters reveal a terrain scarred by countless collisions over billions of years. As planets have evolved, their surfaces have been modified by the impact of orbiting meteoroids and asteroids, leading to the formation of ever more complex and varied craters. The moon's craters provide a clear visual demonstration of how early processes have shaped vast celestial bodies. Orbiting spacecraft have provided invaluable data, enhancing our understanding of these primordial features and the dynamic processes that have sculpted the universe.
